It's that time of the year again, where Lord Gaben (long may He reign) blesses us with discounts and sales. 

To make it easier for everyone to find great games worth their hard-earned money, we're throwing our titles into the ring!

https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/34046344/2db2e49c791d9f436cef4e8d389847bb0b87b90d.png

 Your funny bone requires tickling? Once Upon a Jester will do just that!
 Want to shoot spears made of pure light at weird creatures? Lichtspeer's got your back!


See? There's something for everyone!

And while you're here, you can also check out our upcoming titles:

Techno Banter - an adventure game about being a bouncer guarding the entrance to a techno club. If you think you've got wits and humour to chase the unwanted guests away, test your mettle here!

The Gap - a serious, narrative story about a man fighting to save his own sanity and his family, while delving ever deeper into his past.

If those games pique your interest, it would mean a lot to us if you wishlisted!

Have a great Summer Sale, and may Lord Gaben have mercy on our wallets.

notes.title: MouseCraft 1.1 is live, also a -33% discount!
notes.content:
Hey guys!

Firstly - MouseCraft is currently -33% off and it probably won't be in a similar discount for a longer time, so it's a pretty good time to get it if you still haven't played it.

Secondly - since the launch we have been fixing and adding some stuff, but we didn't feel like they're worth mentioning separately. We thought we will write a bigger post when there's more to tell and I guess now is a good time to do it.

Changelog since launch:


 Updated Steam integration to Steamworks 1.31 and fixed all Linux issues regarding Achievements, Leaderboards and Stats. It will also allow us to add Steam Workshop support in the future.
 Increased the performance and quality of videos for Mac OSX.
 Added full keyboard support - now you can play the game solely with a keyboard.
 Added Xbox gamepad support for Windows and Mac OSX (support for Linux is pretty experimental). Details below.
 Added 2 new languages: Italian and Dutch (thanks to Puxxup and jpelgrom)
 Added Polish descriptions and names for Achievements (thanks to RobeN)
 Added a "language sniffing" mechanism - the game will now set the language according to the operating system language (if there is no other language setting saved already). 
 Optimized a lot of graphics stuff - reduced the number of draw calls by 30%.
 Added functionality to Effects toggle - setting effects to "off" will result in launching the game in a mode suitable for older, low-end computers. 
 Added a green outline showing the currently active Moving Brick.
 Moved all brick outlines to a higher layer so they are more visible during Active Pause.
 Feature cutscenes will no longer appear if you have already completed the level where the feature was introduced.
 Lots of Level Editor bugfixes.


Gamepad support
Windows: Xbox 360 and Xbox One controllers should work out of the box if you have the necessary drivers. A PS3 controller can be used with Motionin Joy application and emulating Xbox 360 controller.
Mac OSX: requires free 3rd party driver by Tattiebogle.
Linux: We're not really sure it will work - it really depends on the drivers.


Oh, and here's a little image showing the controls scheme for Xbox controller:

http://imgur.com/TVDgcRo.jpg

Hope you'll like it!

Cheers,
Crunching Koalas

notes.title: Apparently MouseCraft is one of the most anticipated games of this summer!
notes.content:
Turned out that we are not the only ones that would like MouseCraft to be released as soon as possible!

We just found out that our cheesy game made it to multiple lists of best/biggest/most interesting releases of this month or even the whole summertime!


TIME has put our game in their list of 20 Video Games to keep an eye on during summertime
Digital Spy lists MouseCraft as one of 10 biggest game releases of July
Pocket Gamer thinks MouseCraft is one of 5 most exciting releases on PS Vita this month. They even describe it as a sleeper hit!
Gry-Online thinks that MouseCraft is one of 7 most interesting game releases this month


Well, who are we to disagree?

The final version of MouseCraft launches July 8th, 10 am PST, but you can already get it today by buying the Early Access version , which will obviously upgrade to the full version automatically.

notes.title: MouseCraft Beta is available now!
notes.content:
http://crunchingkoalas.com/downloads/betaAvailable.jpg

The Beta version is ready!

Major changes:

Nearly all previous levels have been redesigned or rearranged (currently 41 levels). These levels won't change in the final game release.
Added Active Pause functionality (now you can freeze time and place the bricks without time pressure)
Destruction Tokens have been replaced with Brick Bombs
Videos, new location and enemies have been added
Support for Achievements, Stats and Steam Cloud has been added
Thousands of bugs has been fixed


Known issues:

Low video performance
Keyboard support is only partially implemented
Level Editor is currently disabled (we are currently working on adding Steam Workshop support)


Few things to note:

Don't worry about the game being finished by July 8th - the rest 39 levels are already made, but we just need a couple more weeks to test them.
Please note the fact that all the levels have been redesigned - it means that all the existing saves will not work.
Linux version still needs more testing, so please report any existing bugs :). Thanks!



See you in the next update!

notes.title: A small Christmas Update!
notes.content:
Hey guys!

We didn't make it with all the changes and fixes before christmas, but at least Schrödinger - our Crazy Cat Scientist has now a christmas hat! Click the link to check it!

Here are some changes we made in this version of the game apart from the hat!

New features:

Added multiple new animations for the Schrodinger - our Crazy Cat Scientist.
Added two new Tetromino bricks: Moving Brick and Indestructible Brick. Check them in the Level Editor!
Added the option to adjust volume of music and sound effects, separately.
Added the option to enable and disable tutorials.

Changes:

Bricks are now destroyed over time when placed in Acid Obstacles.
Water Obstacles conduct electricity produced by Electric Bricks.
Exploding Bricks will now destroy everything within 1-unit range when removed with a Destruction Point.
Level Editor: Reel and Cheese cannot be placed in Water or Acid Obstacles.
Level Editor: Removed the limit where levels must have at least one brick defined.
Level Editor: Added a 99 quantity limit for bricks that are being added to the list.


Bug fixes:

You can hold an extra Tetromino Brick in your hand, when finishing the level, and the game will not crash.
Background animations do not speed up after speeding up the game.
Fixed the bug where Schrodinger appears out of nowhere.
Bricks cannot be destroyed after finishing the level.
The Linux version exits without crashing.
Clicking the Repeat button multiple times will not crash the game.
Optimized Water and Acid Obstacles. They are now renderered in a single draw call.
Optimized electric particles.


10 new levels will be added in the forthcoming days.

Merry Christmas!

Chrunching Koalas
